note: The pair that makes `minimum status` ill-defined. Neither claim dominates.
why: A proved claim restricted to a narrow precondition establishes the law only inside it. A tested claim whose generation domain strictly contains that precondition has been checked over inputs the proof says nothing about. Ranking `proved` above `tested` would let a boundary accept a proof about a region it does not operate in, over evidence about the region it does.
expected: Neither is `the minimum`. A policy stating a threshold cannot express this; a policy stating an ACCEPT SET can.
